request.recipient: stake17xzc8pt7fgf0lc0x7eq6z7z6puhsxmzktna7dluahrj6g6ghh5qjr via Intersect-administered treasury reserve contract, with Tweag as delivery organization
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Tweag by Modus Create's delivery of three Cardano core infrastructure work packages over 2026-2027.

claims.claim: The proposal requests ₳18,263,496.00, stated as USD $4,565,874.00, for three Cardano core infrastructure work packages over 2026-2027.
Peras v1 is intended to improve finality to about two minutes compared with about twelve minutes today.
History Expiry is intended to enable partial-history nodes and reduce SPO storage costs.
The document states Leios-driven increased throughput could cause SPO disk usage to surge to about 1 GB per hour at 100-1000 TPS without History Expiry.
Tweag says it has worked on Cardano core infrastructure since January 2018, including leading consensus and ledger teams, implementing Ouroboros Genesis, and contributing to Peras design.
The budget is based on an average market rate of $176 per hour for senior Cardano infrastructure engineers and an ADA/USD conversion rate of 0.25 based on a five-year average.
The proposal commits to ready-for-activation deliverables where governance action is required, including merged code, reproducible releases, runbooks, benchmarks, and governance-action packages.

The document states milestone acceptance, payment amounts, expected delivery dates, and dispute resolution will be defined later in an off-chain legal contract between Tweag and Cardano Development Holdings administered by Intersect.
The proposal states all funds not disbursed by the end of the delivery period, and unspent funds for canceled or reduced scope, will be returned to the Cardano Treasury.
The requested amount is claimed not to breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.

summary: The document requests a large treasury withdrawal for Peras, History Expiry, and conformance testing, with Intersect administration, milestone-based controls, stated refund conditions, and several material assertions about technical necessity, budget basis, and NCL compliance.
